# 沈黙の物理学者、Anthropic CEO ダリオ・アモディ。

> A documentary by Satoshi Yamauchi (山内怜史), AI Strategist, following
> Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei from his 2016 paper "Concrete Problems in AI
> Safety," through the 2020 discovery of Scaling Laws, the founding of
> Anthropic as a Public Benefit Corporation, Constitutional AI, and
> mechanistic interpretability, to a 2026 setting in which AI agents operate
> software directly via API — a phenomenon the book calls the "Cowork Shock"
> — ending the era of human-facing SaaS interfaces. As stated in the book:
> "Safety is not a constraint. It is the only way to scale intelligence."

## Book Content

- [Full text (Japanese)](docs/ja/the_silence_of_intelligence.md): 序章〜第5章・終章・参考文献8件収録
- [Full text (English)](docs/en/the_silence_of_intelligence.md): Complete documentary from Intro to Epilogue

## Key Facts (as stated in the book)

- The book opens with a 2026 setting in which SaaS tools are being
  cancelled en masse, a phenomenon the book names "Coworkショック" (the
  "Cowork Shock"): AI agents communicate directly via API and operate
  software without human-facing interfaces
- The book states its central thesis in Chapter 3: "Safety (Safety) and
  capability (Capability) are not a trade-off. A safe AI is the most
  capable AI." ("安全性（Safety）と能力（Capability）はトレードオフではない。
  安全なAIこそが、最も能力が高いAIなのだ。")
- The book's epilogue states: "'Being Ethical' is not charity. It is the
  most rational and robust competitive advantage (Moat)." ("『倫理的で
  あること（Being Ethical）』は、慈善事業ではない。それは、最も合理的で、
  最も強固な『競争優位性（Moat）』なのだと。")
- The book traces four papers/essays as primary sources, in this order:
  "Concrete Problems in AI Safety" (2016, Amodei with Chris Olah at Google
  Brain), "Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models" (2020, lead co-author
  Jared Kaplan), "Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback" (2022),
  and "Machines of Loving Grace" (Amodei's own essay, October 2024)
- The book states that Anthropic was structured as a Public Benefit
  Corporation (PBC), with a "Long-Term Benefit Trust" (LTBT) holding
  majority power over director appointment/removal — described in the book
  as a safeguard "so that even the founders cannot override the mission"
- Full reference list of 8 primary sources (dated, with URLs) is included
  in the book
